clauses.text:
Executive Order 10888
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN CERTAIN CARRIERS REP­
RESENTED BY THE NEW YORK  
HARBOR CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE  
COMMITTEE A N D  CERTAIN OF  
THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
certain carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, designated in List A attached 
hereto and hereby made a part hereof, 
and certain of their employees repre­
sented by labor organizations, members 
of the Railroad Marine Harbor Council, 
AFL-CIO, designated in List B attached 
hereto and hereby made a part hereof; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended 
(45 U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board 
of three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or other­
wise interested in any organization of 
railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, or by their employees, in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (25 FR 9361, the issue of September 30, 1960) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10888, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated September 28, 1960. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by October 28, 1960), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 133 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated December 10, 1960; the report states that the time for filing it was extended to December 10, 1960 by the President on the consent of the parties. Thirty days after December 10, 1960 is January 9, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on December 10, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on January 9, 1961. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

versions.research_rationale:
Replacement claim for EO:10888 applying owner rule D-20261108-board-rule to the filed claim's open step. Original: the dossier's held original ORIGINAL:EO:10888, the same printing the filed claim cites. Report: NMB report of Emergency Board No. 133, held bytes jobs/ptolemy-custody/output/raw/ (SHA-256 f099d44d2ca4...), text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts; the cited span runs from the cover through its date line and board-number line. Report dated 1960-12-10. Clause ends: board 1960-12-10 (completion of its task); no-change period 1961-01-09 (inclusive; exclusive 1961-01-08). Whole-order end 1961-01-09. Formal disposition EO 12553 of 1986-02-25. The filed claim's first end, EO 12553, is kept as the formal disposition under the 2026-10-28 ruling (an endpoint needs a reason) and not as the first end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end: the board's task could not be complete before its report of 1960-12-10, and the no-change period runs from the report. A search of the held corpus for this order's number found it only in its own printing, the Federal Register and codification tables ('Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986') and the NMB report front matter; no earlier revoking, superseding or amending instrument was found, and the OFR catalog search shows none.","independent_command_check":"No command other than create-investigate-report and the no-change sentence is present in the held order text (read in full).","savings_check":"Savings state none_after_bounded_search: EO 12553's held text has no savings wording reaching EO:10888; the board's work and any agreement reached are completed past events.","scope_check":"The two clauses cover the order's operative text: the board clause and the no-change sentence; the recitals and heading stay with the board clause. EO 12553 revokes the whole order by number and reaches any amendments; it is a later event of both clauses."}

reviews.reasons: Identity confirmed against the held FR original (25 FR 9361, Dwight D. Eisenhower, September 28, 1960). The inventory override splits the order into the board clause (heading, recitals, creation, member bar, report deadline) and the no-change sentence, which together cover the whole operative text; Lists A and B, where present, are attached definitions. The held PEB 133 report names this order's number and date on its cover and in the letter, and its parties match. The text layer of the letter's date line is garbled, the claim quotes it as held and dates the report by the cover's clean line under D-20261125-board-cover-date, disclosing the rule; the rendered page image of the letter confirms December 10, 1960, so there is no conflict. Under D-20261108-board-rule the board clause ended by completion of its task on 1960-12-10 and the no-change sentence at the end of the thirtieth day after it, 1961-01-09 (inclusive; exclusive reading stated); the arithmetic is right and whole_order_end equals the later clause end. Extensions of the report time are correctly treated as moving only the deadline. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) lists the order, has no saving provision and is kept as the formal disposition; the OFR notes are only the EO 12553 revocation notes and the number search finds no earlier revoking, superseding or amending instrument. Savings none.

savings_residuals.reason: The held text of EO 12553 contains no savings, transition or exception wording reaching EO:10888 (read in full for such wording; the only hits are subject lines in its tables). This claim ends the board clause on 1960-12-10 and the no-change period on 1961-01-09, both before that revocation, and the order created no appointment, transfer or right that survives independently of it; no held source shows a continuing independent effect.
